references.text: Summarizes the creation of heaven and earth, as a conclusion to what is introduced in 1:1.
By the Lord's word the heavens were made – an echo of the creative act in Genesis 1:1.
Thanks the Lord who made the heavens with understanding, a praise of the work of creation described in Genesis 1:1.
God the Lord who made the heavens and stretched out the earth – a direct parallel to the creation in Genesis 1:1.
Jeremiah acknowledges God as the creator of heaven and earth, in line with Genesis 1:1.
'In the beginning was the Word' – a direct parallel to 'In the beginning' in Genesis 1:1, and all things were made through the Word.
All things were created by Christ and for him, both in heaven and on earth – an elaboration of the creation in Genesis 1:1.
By faith we understand that the world was formed by God's word, reflecting the creative word in Genesis 1:1.
God is praised as the creator of all things – a praise that points back to the creation in Genesis 1:1.
A direct quote identifying Jesus as the same creator as in Genesis 1:1.
An additional theological perspective on the timing of creation and the role of wisdom.
Expands the understanding of the Creator's nature (power and wisdom) behind the creation in 1:1.
Theological confirmation of God's identity as the creator of heaven and earth.
Repeats and confirms the Creator's wisdom and power as the foundation for creation.
Uses creation as a basis for blessing and God's identity.
Prophetic confirmation of God's sovereignty as the sole Creator of heaven and earth.
Summarizes creation and confirms God's sovereignty and life-giving power.
Interpretation of creation through wisdom and insight, complementing 1:1.
Expands on 'in the beginning' with a reflection on God's eternity before creation.
Direct reference to creation as the work of God's hands.
Contrasts idols with God's unique role as Creator of heaven.
Repeats and confirms God's sovereignty as the sole Creator of heaven.
Complements creation with God's purpose that the earth should be inhabited.
Identifies the Word as the one who was present at creation in 'the beginning'.
Identifies Christ as the Creator of all things in heaven and on earth.
Emphasizes God's almighty power in creating the earth, humans, and animals.
Identifies the Word as the one who was present at creation in 'the beginning'.
Confirms God's sovereignty over creation established by Him.
Links God's help to His role as Creator of heaven and earth.
Links God's help to His role as Creator of heaven and earth.
Complements the creation event with a timeframe of six days.
Identifies the creation of humanity as part of the original creation.
